title: TNS: Render Oracle typed row and bind values
description:
Follow-up to the merged OCI-call-decoding series (TTI_IOV/DCB/RXH/ALL8/
FETCH/LOBOPS and the RXD row-value framings). That work extracted row and
bind values as raw fields; this renders them as human-readable typed values
through a single shared decoder used by both the row (TTI_RXD) and bind
(TTI_ALL8) paths.

- Name the OCI call in the Info column.
- NUMBER rendered as a decimal.
- DATE / TIMESTAMP / TIMESTAMP LTZ rendered as a datetime.
- BINARY_FLOAT / BINARY_DOUBLE rendered locale-independently
  (g_ascii_formatd).
- VARCHAR / CHAR / STRING rendered as text.
- Bind values routed through the same shared decoder as row values.

A final commit names the Oracle datatype codes: the switch and comparisons
used bare numbers with the meaning only in a comment, though tns_data_types[]
already listed every name. They now share TNS_DATATYPE_* constants (distinct
from the packet-level TNS_TYPE_*), and the JSON and VECTOR rows missing from
the table are added, so those columns show their type name instead of
"unknown".

The _gen_tns_rxd_types fixture is extended to cover the rendered types, with
matching assertions in test/suite_dissection.py. All decoders target the
Oracle 11g wire shape.

notes.body: added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 3

commits_data.title: TNS: Name the Oracle datatype codes
commits_data.message:
TNS: Name the Oracle datatype codes

The value decoder switched and compared bare datatype numbers - 2 for
NUMBER, 109 for an object, 112/113 for CLOB/BLOB and so on - with the
meaning carried only in a trailing comment, even though tns_data_types[]
already spelled out every name.

Define the Oracle datatype codes once and use them in tns_data_types[], in
dissect_tns_value()'s switch and its scalar render dispatch, and in the
CLOB/BLOB bind handling, so a code lives in a single place. The names use a
TNS_DATATYPE_ prefix to avoid the existing TNS_TYPE_ packet-type constants;
python-oracledb lists most of these as its ORA_TYPE_NUM_* constants.

Row and bind rendering is otherwise unchanged; the JSON and VECTOR rows
that were missing from the table now show their type name instead of
"unknown".

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: TNS: Render bind values with the shared value decoder
commits_data.message:
TNS: Render bind values with the shared value decoder

Generalise the per-type row-value decoder (dissect_tns_rxd_value ->
dissect_tns_value, taking a header field and a label prefix) and reuse
it for the TTI_ALL8 bind values, which previously showed only raw bytes.

Bind values now render like row values — "Bind 1 (VARCHAR): hi",
"Bind 2 (NUMBER): 10" — decoded by each bind's declared type (NUMBER,
DATE/TIMESTAMP, BINARY_FLOAT/DOUBLE, VARCHAR/CHAR/STRING), while the raw
bytes stay in tns.data_bind.value. A bind of a type the decoder does not
frame (ROWID/LONG/LOB/object/JSON/VECTOR) stops the row, as for rows.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: TNS: Render VARCHAR / CHAR / STRING row values as text
commits_data.message:
TNS: Render VARCHAR / CHAR / STRING row values as text

Character-column row values (VARCHAR type 1, STRING 5, CHAR 96) were
shown only as raw hex bytes. Render them as text in the column's tree
label (e.g. "Column 2 (VARCHAR): hi"), decoding the value bytes as the
session charset (ordinarily UTF-8); the raw bytes stay in
tns.data_col.value.

National (AL16UTF16) columns and chunked (long) values are left raw for
now — the csform is not threaded into the row decoder and a chunked
value's bytes interleave chunk lengths.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: TNS: Render BINARY_FLOAT / BINARY_DOUBLE row values
commits_data.message:
TNS: Render BINARY_FLOAT / BINARY_DOUBLE row values

Decode BINARY_FLOAT (type 100, 4 bytes) and BINARY_DOUBLE (type 101,
8 bytes) row values from Oracle's order-preserving IEEE-754 form and
show them in the column's tree label (e.g. "Column 5 (BINARY_FLOAT):
1.5"); the raw bytes stay in tns.data_col.value.

The stored form is order-preserving: if the high bit is set it was
positive (clear it), otherwise it was negative (invert every bit), then
read as big-endian IEEE-754. The result is formatted with
g_ascii_formatd() so the decimal separator is always '.', independent of
the runtime locale.

The mixed-type RXD fixture gains BINARY_FLOAT and BINARY_DOUBLE columns
(1.5 and 2.25) to exercise it.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: TNS: Render Oracle DATE / TIMESTAMP row values
commits_data.message:
TNS: Render Oracle DATE / TIMESTAMP row values

Following the NUMBER rendering, decode DATE (type 12), TIMESTAMP (180)
and TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE (231) row values to a datetime
string shown in the column's tree label (e.g. "Column 4 (DATE):
2024-01-15 10:30:00"); the raw bytes stay in tns.data_col.value.

The decoder implements the packed form: 7 bytes hold century+100,
year+100, month, day, hour+1, minute+1, second+1; an 11-byte value adds
4-byte big-endian nanoseconds. TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE (181, with its
trailing offset bytes) is left raw for now.

The mixed-type RXD fixture gains a DATE column to exercise it.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: TNS: Render Oracle NUMBER row values as decimal
commits_data.message:
TNS: Render Oracle NUMBER row values as decimal

A NUMBER column value in a TTI_RXD row was shown only as its raw
base-100 bytes (e.g. c1 0b). Decode it to a decimal string and show it
in the column's tree label (e.g. "Column 1 (NUMBER): 10"), while the raw
bytes stay in the filterable tns.data_col.value field.

The decoder implements the base-100 form: byte 0 is the biased
exponent with the sign in its top bit (inverted for negatives), the rest
are base-100 mantissa groups (negatives carry a trailing 0x66
terminator), and 0x80 is zero. Placement of the decimal point follows
the exponent. Other numeric renderings (DATE, TIMESTAMP, ...) remain
raw for now.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: TNS: Name the OCI call in the Info column
commits_data.message:
TNS: Name the OCI call in the Info column

Every TTC function call (SQLNET_USER_OCI_FUNC) rendered in the packet
list only as the generic "User OCI Functions", so a commit, a fetch, an
execute and a logoff were indistinguishable without expanding the tree.

Append the specific call name from the OCI sub-function table to the
Info column, e.g. "User OCI Functions (Fetch a Row)" / "(Commit)" /
"(Generic authentication call)". The execute and LOB paths still add
their SQL text / opcode after it.

Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>
